verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const r=(f)=>fs.existsSync(f)?fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8"):"";const die=(m)=>{console.error("LIVE-695: "+m);process.exit(1)};if(!/"@react-email\/render"/.test(r("package.json")))die("React Email is not a dependency");if(!/export function EmailShell/.test(r("lib/email-react/shell.tsx")))die("there is no React Email base template");const re=r("lib/billing/receipt-email.ts");if(!/renderEmail\(/.test(re)||!/ReceiptEmail/.test(re)||/emailShell\(/.test(re))die("the receipt family is still a hand-built string template");const g=r("lib/billing/receipt-email.golden.test.ts");if(!/visible\.txt/.test(g))die("no golden test pins what a member receives");for(const id of ["order-buyer","seller-notice","donation-guest"])for(const ext of ["html","txt","visible.txt"])if(!fs.existsSync("lib/billing/__golden__/"+id+"."+ext))die("missing golden "+id+"."+ext);console.log("ok")'

append.detail: React Email is the renderer (@react-email/render, no component kit). lib/email-react/shell.tsx is the base template, the same wrapper emailShell writes and reading its own style constants; lib/email-react/receipt.tsx is the receipt family's body, so every money receipt and the earner notice render through it. lib/billing/receipt-email.golden.test.ts pins the HTML and text byte for byte, and the words a reader sees against a capture taken from the string template before the move: identical. Other email families move onto the base template one family at a time.
